question: A function signature changes in module A, and callers in modules B and C are updated inconsistently, causing a runtime mismatch. Per-file passes each judged their own file correct in isolation and missed the mismatch. Which review step should have caught this, and why?
options: A) The self-review step performed by the generator, since it still remembers why it changed the signature and can check callers from memory
B) A second per-file pass over module A alone, since re-reading the same file twice increases the chance of noticing the signature change
C) The cross-file integration pass, because it traces data flow and interface usage across files rather than analyzing each file alone
D) A longer per-file pass that reads both module A and module B together in one sitting rather than as two separate local passes
correct_answers: C) The cross-file integration pass, because it traces data flow and interface usage across files rather than analyzing each file alone
explanations: Incorrect. The generator's self-review carries the same retained-reasoning limitation and is not the mechanism designed to catch cross-file inconsistencies.
Incorrect. Repeating a per-file pass on module A alone still never examines how modules B and C actually call it.
Correct. An integration pass is designed to trace how data and interfaces flow across files, which is exactly the kind of mismatch a per-file pass, scoped to one file at a time, cannot see.
Incorrect. Ad hoc combining of two files into one longer per-file pass isn't the designed cross-file mechanism and doesn't scale to the full callers set including module C.
